steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

ET is UTC-4 in September (EDT, as DST applies). Madrid is CEST (UTC+2) in September. The offset is therefore +6 hours.

September 30, 2026, 17:00 ET becomes 23:00 the same day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru (Lima) uses PET, which is UTC-5 year-round (no DST).  
July 15 12:00 UTC is therefore 07:00 the same day in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT (UTC-7). Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in October, so add 9 hours.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the CET/CEST time zone. March 3, 2026 falls during standard time (CET, UTC+1), so the 11:59 PM PST (UTC-8) deadline converts to 08:59 the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles is PST (UTC-8) in February (standard time, before DST starts). The time difference is 9 hours behind.

10:00 CET on Feb 2 converts to 01:00 PST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Lima, Peru uses PET (UTC-5) with no DST in 2026. The offset difference is 14 hours (JST is 14h ahead).

8:00 AM JST on 2026-05-05 is therefore 2026-05-04 at 18:00 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific Time (UTC-7, as DST is in effect in late October). Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in October, which is a 9-hour difference ahead of PT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

First, convert ET (UTC-4 on October 30, as DST ends Nov 1 2026) to UTC: 9:00 AM ET = 13:00 UTC.  
Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in late October, so add 1 hour: 14:00.  
The date remains the same.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific Time (UTC-7, as DST is in effect in November). Madrid uses Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) with no DST in early November, resulting in an 8-hour difference.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 20, 2026 23:59 PT is 8 hours ahead in Madrid (CET, no DST yet in March).  
ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET is 03:00 AM PDT in Los Angeles (CET is UTC+1, PDT is UTC-7; 12-hour difference).

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 03:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the CEST time zone (UTC+2). 12:00 AM ET on 2026-10-12 is 2026-10-12 00:00 EDT (UTC-4), which converts to 2026-10-12 06:00 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**  
October 9, 2026 at 23:59 AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to the latest possible time zone on Earth, which is UTC−12:00. Madrid, Spain uses Central European Summer Time (CEST = UTC+2) in October. The difference is 14 hours, so 23:59 UTC−12 on Oct 9 equals 13:59 UTC+2 on Oct 10.

**ANSWER:** 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT is Pacific Time (UTC-7 in summer 2026, as August falls in PDT). Madrid is in CEST (UTC+2). The difference is 9 hours ahead.

12:00 PM PT on August 14, 2026 converts to 21:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

First, Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45. Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5. The difference is exactly 10 hours and 45 minutes, with Lima being behind Nepal.

April 2, 2026, at 17:00 NPT converts as follows:  
17:00 minus 10 hours = 07:00 on the same day, then minus 45 minutes = 06:15.  
No date change occurs.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**  
Adelaide uses Australian Central Standard Time (ACST, UTC+9:30) and does not observe daylight saving on October 6. Madrid uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in October. The time difference is therefore 7 hours and 30 minutes (Adelaide is ahead).  
10:00 ACST on 2026-10-06 is 02:30 CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 02:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is AEDT (UTC+11) on October 3, 2026. Madrid is CEST (UTC+2). The time difference is 9 hours (Sydney ahead).

6:00 PM Sydney = 09:00 Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
